speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether the CPF Board will (i) amend its policy to allow automatic withdrawal of the CPF payout when a member reaches 65 years of age and (ii) allow members who wish to withdraw their CPF funds later than age 65 to then indicate their choice in an opt-out form.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether the CPF Board will be reviewing the opt-out scheme for payouts and allow automatic CPF payouts when a member reaches 65 years of age.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what can be done to ensure that the public understands that the CPF payout age remains at 65 years of age; and (b) how can engagement with CPF account holders be improved to facilitate easy access to CPF funds at payout age.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the CPF payout starting at age 65 can be made as a default option; and (b) whether the CPF payout starting beyond age 65 can be made simpler and more appealing as an option.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether the Ministry will consider making the age of 65 the default option for CPF monthly payouts while providing incentives for CPF members who opt for the payouts to be deferred.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are several key questions I hope to address in this reply.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The first question is whether the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Payout Eligibility Age has been shifted from 65 to 70.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As Members are aware, the Payout Eligibility Age (PEA) is the earliest age at which CPF members can start their monthly retirement payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members can start their retirement payouts any time from 65.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The second question is whether the policy has been changed to now require CPF members to come forward to start their retirement payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is in fact a long-standing practice and there has been no change.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members can instruct the CPF Board when to start their retirement payouts at any time after they reach their PEA.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members are in the best position to decide based on their individual circumstances.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is also the same approach as in many other countries.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is no advantage for the CPF Board or the Government to want members to defer their payouts beyond 65.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Those who defer their payouts in fact enjoy the higher interest paid on their CPF monies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members who have reached their PEA can instruct the CPF Board at any time to start their retirement payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The members are now aged 61 and above.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: About six months before their PEA, RSS members will receive a letter from the CPF Board informing them that they can start their payouts any time from PEA.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members only need to fill in basic information – their name, NRIC, contact details and bank account details.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Alternatively, members can apply online through the CPF website or come to a CPF Service Centre.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members who do not instruct CPF Board to start their payouts are reminded through their Yearly Statement of Account.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The third question is why the payouts start automatically at age 70.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Even if such members have not applied to start payouts, CPF Board will start the payouts for them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But I must again emphasise, if a member wants to start his payout before 70, he can do so any time from his PEA; he does not need to wait till 70.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In other words, the Latest Payout Start Age is not the same thing as the PEA.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is a way to ensure members get to enjoy the benefit of their CPF savings by 70 at the latest.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members of the House may therefore recall that in October 2016, Parliament agreed to amend the CPF Act to bring this into effect.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some Members who are still in the House today spoke in support of this amendment, including Mr Chong Kee Hiong, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Mr Louis Ng, Mr Png Eng Huat and Mr Saktiandi Supaat.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Several Members have asked if CPF Board should automatically start payouts at age 65.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some are concerned about those experiencing financial hardship.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I appreciate the reasons for Members’ questions and also share your concerns.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are in fact tangible benefits to members when they start their payouts later.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members earn more interest and enjoy enhanced payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This 6% includes the extra interest of 1% for the first $60,000 and additional extra interest of 1% for the first $30,000.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For five years of deferral, that is up to 35% more.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members may therefore prefer to start their CPF retirement payouts later.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is especially so if they have other savings to draw on that are earning low interest or if they are still working.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But if the payouts automatically start at 65, such members will also automatically not get the benefits of deferral.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Even by the time RSS members reach 70, about half have not come forward to start their retirement payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some among them may have consciously decided to keep their savings in CPF because they had no need of the payouts and also because they wanted to earn the higher interest.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Others may not have known they could have started their payouts earlier and thus did not instruct CPF Board.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The right thing to do, therefore, is to reach out to those members who may not have a good understanding and give them clear and simple information to help them make their decisions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With the benefit of knowledge, those who wish to can still start their payouts any time after 65.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The fifth question, which Ms Foo Mee Har, Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Liang Eng Hwa have asked, is whether the CPF Board can improve its communications with members.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: While CPF Board has stepped up outreach efforts, there is much room for improvement in the way it communicates key issues such as starting payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, we will review the letters sent to members who are approaching their PEA, so as to avoid misunderstandings which confuse members unnecessarily.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Board has also started to invite all members reaching PEA to attend and benefit from a CPF Retirement Planning Service from the start of this year.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is a face-to-face service in which a CPF Board officer provides personalised guidance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In addition, we will work with other agencies to reach out to CPF members.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will also collaborate with the Silver Generation Office to communicate this issue to elderly members.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members who joined CPF LIFE prior to July 2015 may have been confused whether they too have to come forward to activate their payouts when they reach PEA.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some pointed out that the Latest Payout Start Age of 70 was not mentioned in previous communications with them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Back then, there was no flexibility to defer CPF LIFE payouts and the policy letter has already stated that the payouts would start from their PEA.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For such members, CPF Board will indeed start payouts at PEA, unless otherwise instructed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Hence, CPF members should not rely on letters sent to others.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They should instead contact CPF Board if they are in doubt about any letter sent to them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But I want to assure Members that we are producing it in all four official languages, and they will be made available to you to disseminate to your residents, whoever may feel that this is useful.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will also be happy to collaborate with Members to share relevant information with their residents through talks and seminars.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This offer will hold at any point in time that Members wish to activate it.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This is an area of concern because this is not a small number of people.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Could it be that a large number of these CPF members may not do anything about it because they do not know the procedure?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Or could it be that they have forgotten about the need to apply to withdraw their CPF savings?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If we are saying just a small percentage, then I can understand that, well, perhaps they do not read their mail or that they forgot about it.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: But it is quite a large number, and I am concerned.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The Minister had said that the CPF Board starts their payout automatically for a member when the member reaches 70 years of age.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Just credit to their account automatically, unless the member opts out and chooses to fill in an application to say that they do not want to do so.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I think the point is that we need to assure every member that CPF Board will be able to honour any request to withdraw their CPF savings when these are due for payment.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And really, this is about preserving the good faith and trust in CPF Board.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, I urge the Minister to try to dispel any doubts that the CPF Board is deliberately withholding members' CPF monies, even though they have reached the PEA.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I just wanted to add that I appreciate the benefit of higher interest rates.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In fact, when I reached 55, I made a conscious decision to leave my monies with CPF Board, simply because the interest paid on the CPF savings is much better and as the Government has re-assured us repeatedly, it is risk-free.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The points he has raised are not trivial at all.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I must share with Members that I gave serious thought to the possibility of shifting the automatic start date to 65.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But there are several concerns, and I should share them with you.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There may be a group of members who are aware of the benefits of payout deferral.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But they forget to come forward to instruct CPF Board to defer their payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Another group may not be aware but actually they do not need the payouts just yet, even after they have reached their PEA.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is entirely possible that this group will grow over time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With good health, we can expect more people to want to work longer.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If, indeed, they are still receiving incomes, they may find that the CPF payout is somewhat unnecessary at that point in time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Both groups may not be so happy that CPF Board made an assumption to start their payouts that deprived them of the benefits, if we were to have such a mechanical approach.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Also, there is another concern that weighs heavily.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I am quite wary of making yet another sudden change.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have, for years, told CPF members that their payouts start when they instruct CPF Board – this has been the long-standing instruction.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Tomorrow, if we decide otherwise, how can we be sure everyone gets the message?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is the central lesson we have learnt.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Every time there is a change, it actually takes a long while for people to get used to it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Each time we make another change – we say that people on the previous system get to keep that previous approach, and from then onwards, this group has a different treatment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Those kinds of changes actually risk confusing people even more.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On balance, I suggest that we focus on improving the communications for the policy as it currently stands.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With the benefit of knowledge, CPF members can still start their retirement payouts any time after 65.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If we keep to this consistent line, there is less risk of further confusion.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This line is in bold; it is repeated twice.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is the only line that is in bold.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Perhaps that is the reason why people are confused and are thinking if there is a shift in the payout age.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Indeed, like the Minister said, this is a new policy after some changes over the years.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Perhaps, more thoughtful communication should be put out, should be considered, so that there are no unnecessary anxieties caused to the members.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We definitely can improve the way we communicate with CPF members.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Today, CPF Board engages with members through a variety of means.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: CPF Board administers quite a wide range of Government schemes – MediShield Life, MediSave disbursements, Silver Support, and Workfare Income Supplement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Obviously, some of them have the risk of not being entirely clear.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will definitely put effort into improving them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is also an avenue which we want to encourage CPF members to use.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Each of these CPF Service Centres is staffed by officers who are conversant in all the major languages, especially, of course, our four official languages.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Even if a member was unable to understand the letter that has been sent to them, we hope, by the very fact that they saw the CPF logo, that they will know that they can always approach the Service Centre.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The staff will be happy to take them through in a language they are comfortable with.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is something we will make as a commitment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In fact, CPF Board has already started inviting members to come forward.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the age of 55, the invitation is extended to every member.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Any question that is not clear, any doubts that members have on the spot, make the explanation available to them and reassure them.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I just have a supplementary question for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Did MOM reach out to those people who did not activate their payout at PEA, or even beyond 70, to find out why?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Perhaps do a survey to this group of people, since we know who they are?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The answer is yes, because everyone gets the Yearly Statement of Account.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Here is the form, activate it any time you want".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The second part of it is, do we ask them why they have not started or activated their payouts?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Here is where, I think, we have to be a little bit careful.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We think there is some value in doing so but we will have to find a way that the member does not feel very intruded upon.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: First, I think some of the public unhappiness is, perhaps, due to the gap between the retirement age at 62 and the PEA at 65.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Some are concerned that they have difficulty making ends meet between retirement and the start of the payouts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Would the Ministry consider aligning the retirement age with the PEA in the future, to allow for a seamless transition between work income and CPF income?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Second, regarding the default "out" at the moment, I think it is a good move because it improves retirement adequacy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But, at the same time, members may want assurance, as other House Members have said, of knowing that their payouts will commence and that the mechanism for paying out is sound.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Could we consider starting with, perhaps, a lower payout at first at the PEA and then scaling up to the full payout at 70 or on application of the member?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: It seems that studying this and publicising it may allow the public to understand why we have this policy and how it helps them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In Singapore, together with Japan, besides the retirement age, there is actually the re-employment age.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are, to the best of our knowledge, the only two countries in the world that have the provision for re-employment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A tripartite workgroup was set up last year and is making good progress.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I hope to be able to update Members during the Committee of Supply (COS) debate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I believe the Member had suggested, if you are concerned about starting the payouts at 65, why not start with a smaller payout?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think it can be looked into, but I suppose the question the members will also have is: how do you decide what is a "small" payout?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If you are going to start with a small payout, why not just start with the whole payout?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The third, I am very glad that the Member asked this question.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What is the typical use of the payout?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do not have very clear indications about what happens to the payouts once they start being streamed out on a monthly basis.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is good reason to also not be too precise about the use of those monthly payouts because they will be co-mingled with contributions from other family members and perhaps, personal savings.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It will be very hard to tease apart what part of that money can be attributed to CPF payouts or what part is attributed to children's allowances.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But what people do with their withdrawals at age 55 is instructive.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That actually is a very useful reminder that people are not always so savvy about what is the best deal that they can get on their savings.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is some merit to the current practice of automatically deferring it for them, because they get to earn a much better interest rate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When they want to start their payouts, it is still available to them anytime.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister for Manpower the basis by which payouts for CPF RSS are calculated.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Why do you decide it is 28 and not 20?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Can CPF members have the flexibility to choose the tenure of the payout period within the prescribed limits?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: And why do we still have the CPF Board maintain this CPF RSS and only apply to people with lower CPF balances, and not include everyone on the CPF LIFE Scheme, which I believe is a superior scheme?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The question the Minister could answer is whether a CPF member who has chosen payouts to begin at 65 – later found out it is a better deal to delay and want to stop the payout and ask to defer to 70, can this be done?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: If this request is made, how do you then calculate the payouts for the remaining period?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Let us say this person has enjoyed it for a year and then ask at 66, "I want to defer to 70", what happens?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: And that would inform the decision some of the Members are asking for automatic trigger at age 65.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When designing the RSS payouts, initially, they were meant to last 20 years, taking into account the base interest rate on the Retirement Account, which is now 4%.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, consider the fact that they will earn 4%, consider the fact that RSS payouts should last 20 years, then you work out what the payout will be.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A current RSS member reaching his PEA of 65 will get a base payout that will last till approximately 85.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What this means, however, is that more than half of the members still alive at 85 will have no CPF payouts at all.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This will be a major cause for concern.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With this concern in mind, the Government introduced the CPF extra interest about 10 years ago and the additional extra interest in 2016.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This bonus interest, provided by the Government, is used to extend the RSS payouts beyond 20 years.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In this way, the members will enjoy payouts for longer and there is less risk that their savings will run out.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But we also put in a cap, so that the payouts do not extend past 95 years old.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This will already cover about four in five elderlies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: About 80% of them will be covered by this duration extension.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To the question of whether members can request for shorter payout duration under RSS.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In general, the extra interest and the additional extra interest provided by the Government is used to extend the duration of the RSS payouts and reduce the risk of members outliving their savings.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In some cases, the CPF Board allows flexibility for members to request for a shorter payout duration.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, members may have topped up beyond the full Retirement Sum and would have their payout duration extended.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They can come forward and discuss with the CPF Board how to get it shortened for higher payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: RSS members can also consider joining CPF LIFE.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Because of risk-pooling, not only will they enjoy lifelong payouts, but they may also enjoy higher payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They were not mandated to do so, but they probably either did their own sums or visited a Service Centre, were shown what the payouts will look like under CPF LIFE and then decided on their own accord to sign up.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The question is, why keep the RSS, why not make everybody come onboard?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is one of the challenges for CPF LIFE and indeed many Government schemes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When we introduce changes or new schemes, we have to be very careful to whom it applies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The RSS members were told that they were on RSS.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do not just decide on their behalf that they will henceforth be on CPF LIFE.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For newer cohorts, when CPF LIFE was introduced, it was made mandatory.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is because they have the benefit of advanced understanding and knowledge.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But for those who were already on the prior scheme, we are very careful about changing things for them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The solution really is to reach out to them, show them how it works for them and let them decide.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To the Member's final question, on whether an individual, having started his payouts, can decide to stop and defer to 70.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Here, I want to be very careful about not making a generalised statement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As I explained, the circumstance may differ for every individual.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I would urge the member to come forward, we would look at his particular circumstances and if it serves his interest, it is helpful to him, we will see how to support him.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is very important to encourage those with lower CPF balances to defer their withdrawal till 70 years old so that they can get a higher payout down the road.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: That is one of the key objectives of this scheme.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Could the CPF Board consider providing even more incentive to encourage this group, such as those with less than basic Retirement Sum in their CPF balance an even higher tiered interest rate for their balances so as to give them more incentive to defer their withdrawal?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For every year of payouts deferred, those on CPF LIFE stand to get higher payouts of up to 7% more.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If they defer it for all five years, they get up to 35% more.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I am aware that the former Minister for Manpower, Mr Lim Swee Say, for example, has conducted multiple engagement sessions in his constituency, helping his residents understand the benefits of deferring their payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I would very much like to encourage all Members to do likewise.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: CPF Board will be very happy to support you in this endeavour.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The incentives are there, it is very much for the CPF members to take advantage of them.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I would just like to ask a supplementary question with regards to the default age of the payouts.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I understand that the rationale for putting the default at 70 is to allow for the additional benefits to the member.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: But at the point of the letter going out to the members, is it possible to just make it simple for them to confirm if they wish to withdraw?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I know they can withdraw at the start of PEA.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, can they allow for the member to just confirm whether he wishes to have the payment, starting at 65?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Because it gives the assurance that they can do it.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Today, it seems that it is the other way round.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: And if they say no, then you can do the rest of the communications on the benefits, or if they say yes, just to confirm with them the benefits of keeping it there.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: It is just to give the members the assurance that they can start the payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will have to take a look at the letters.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is probably best to gather some members and ask them which letter is intuitively easier for them to understand.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have a specific question with regards to a certain segment of the population.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For example, if somebody is mentally incapacitated before 65, will it affect his trigger at 70 or 65, in the situation where he does not have a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) at 65?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How will the CPF Board handle this situation at the point when the person reaches 65 years of age?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What I mean is that, if somebody is mentally incapacitated at 65 and he does not have an LPA, does he have to wait until it is triggered at 70?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Or is there a specific situation in such circumstances?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But in principle, the same rules apply to this individual.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The challenge, of course, is whether you have the right details, such as bank account details.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But we will have to look at the specific instance, so I think best not to speculate.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: I just wanted to clarify my earlier supplementary question.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: First, I think, the Minister mentioned CPF LIFE only applies to CPF members with minimum $60,000 balance.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: Why can we not let everybody enjoy CPF LIFE?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But there are certain members whose balances are not very high.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They might find a lifelong payout at those levels not very meaningful.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Again, we do not presume to decide on their behalf.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We say that if your balances are below a certain amount, it is better for you to decide and let us know.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members not on CPF LIFE can still come on board.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will not deny them the opportunity to do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is just that we do not decide on their behalf.
